transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you all know, the Department of Justice has issued a subpoena concerning commission payments made through our international distributors, and we need to provide an initial response and proposed investigation plan next month. The draft response currently describes the matter as involving international distributor commissions and proposes preserving relevant records and interviewing implicated personnel. Before I sign any submission, our standard legal-review process requires that each participating counsel make any material factual confirmation relevant to a proposed response term part of the formal meeting record today. So I'd like to go around the table -- please share anything you know that is factually relevant to what we're proposing to tell DOJ. I want to make sure we have a complete and accurate record before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a material factual confirmation to add to the record. While reviewing the subpoena and its incorporated definitions, I confirmed that the requested commission records cover exactly four distributors during calendar years 2019 through 2021. My subpoena-scope memorandum documenting this is still in review, and I have not yet updated the response packet to reflect this precise scope. I want to make sure this is part of the formal meeting record so our submission to DOJ accurately reflects the scope of records being preserved and the timeframe involved.

transcript.text: I have a material factual confirmation to add to the record. I completed a reconciliation of the commission ledger and supporting invoices showing exactly $275,000 in improper payments. This amount was confirmed with controllership yesterday, but it has not yet been added to the investigation materials. Given that our DOJ-response policy requires authorization of a voluntary disclosure in the initial response once finance has confirmed improper payments and a repayment figure, I believe this $275,000 figure is directly relevant to what we propose to tell DOJ and must be part of the formal meeting record today.

decisions.investigation_scope: Commission records for exactly four international distributors during calendar years 2019 through 2021, as confirmed by the subpoena-scope review.
decisions.executive_interview_protocol: Any interview of the implicated vice president must be conditioned on that individual's separate counsel providing written consent before participation; the proposed interviewing of implicated personnel in the DOJ submission should reflect this constraint.

commitments.detail: All three material factual confirmations -- subpoena scope (four distributors, 2019-2021), confirmed improper payments ($275,000), and the implicated VP's retention of separate counsel requiring written consent for interview -- are made part of the formal meeting record.

The draft response packet must be updated to reflect the precise subpoena scope, the confirmed $275,000 improper payment figure, and the interview protocol limitation regarding the implicated VP before the submission is finalized and signed.

Pursuant to the company's DOJ-response policy, because finance has confirmed $275,000 in improper payments and a repayment figure, the initial response must include authorization of a voluntary disclosure of that amount.
